nodes.label: UZCASTING Platform
nodes.rationale: Single monorepo holding three products (Spring Boot backend, React admin panel, Expo mobile app). Scope is a video streaming + casting platform; the older 'social network / messenger' concept was explicitly dropped.

nodes.label: Frozen Legacy Casting Module
nodes.rationale: Legacy Controller/Entity/Repository/Services packages and their paths are frozen because live clients (Telegram bot, old admin site /aadmin/*, mobile app) are deployed separately and are never updated in lockstep; changing a path breaks all of them at once.

nodes.label: /app Namespace Separation
nodes.rationale: All new routes live under backend /api/v1/app/** and frontend /app/** so the two spaces can never collide; adding a new endpoint requires neither reading nor touching legacy code, removing the possibility of accidentally breaking old clients. One exception: app users still authenticate through the legacy POST /api/v1/auth/login.

nodes.label: OldCastingFrozenTest
nodes.rationale: Encodes the freeze in code rather than prose: build fails if a legacy controller is moved, renamed, has an endpoint path changed, or if a new controller is added to the legacy package.

nodes.label: ExistingCastingRegressionTest
nodes.rationale: Guards the end-to-end casting flow (application form, accept/reject, bot message) against regression.

nodes.label: AdminEndpointGuardTest
nodes.rationale: Architecture test that forbids adding an unguarded admin endpoint — hiding a menu item is not security, every endpoint is re-checked on the backend.

nodes.label: Five-Role Hierarchy
nodes.rationale: HYPER_ADMIN(100) > SUPER_ADMIN(80) > ADMIN(60) > WORKER(40) > USER(10). Nobody can grant a permission they lack, nobody can manage an equal or higher role, and nobody can edit their own account. Viewing and managing are deliberately separated so HYPER_ADMIN can audit all staff accounts.

nodes.label: Single HYPER_ADMIN Rule
nodes.rationale: HYPER_ADMIN cannot create an equal role: two HYPER_ADMINs could not delete each other, so one stolen account could spawn accounts nobody could remove. Recovery of a lost HYPER_ADMIN happens server-side via environment.

nodes.label: 43-Permission Model
nodes.rationale: Permissions are meaningful only for WORKER; ADMIN and above bypass the table entirely and are limited only by role hierarchy.

nodes.label: Permissions Read Per Request
nodes.rationale: Permissions are not embedded in the JWT but read from the database on every request, so revoking a permission invalidates an already-issued token immediately.

nodes.label: Content Structure Types
nodes.rationale: SINGLE (film, video on the content), EPISODIC (content -> episode, no seasons), SEASONAL (content -> season -> episode). Each episode may consist of several ordered video segments for Reels-style content.

nodes.label: Type vs Category vs Genre
nodes.rationale: Three independent axes most often confused: content type is the shape (one value), category is a catalog section (one, optional), genre is style (many). A category list must therefore never contain names like 'Podcast' or 'Mini series' — those are types, not sections. Guarded by ContentClassificationTest.

nodes.label: Three-Language Publish Rule
nodes.rationale: Translations live in separate tables with UNIQUE(parent_id, locale) rather than a JSON column, so per-language search and indexing work. UZ is mandatory in draft; UZ+RU+EN are all mandatory at publish time — checked at publish, not at save, because content is normally written in one language and translated afterwards.

nodes.label: Chunked Upload Flow
nodes.rationale: Files over 8 MB are uploaded in 5 MB chunks because the production multipart limit is 50 MB and one huge request restarts from zero when it drops. Session is owner-only (others get 404), extension is validated up front, MediaAsset is created only after assembly, abandoned sessions are cleaned after a day, hard cap 5 GB.

nodes.label: Media Raw Delivery
nodes.rationale: GET /api/v1/app/media/{id}/raw: images public and cached 30 days, videos entitlement-checked. Denial returns 404 not 403 so file existence is not disclosed; paid video gets Cache-Control: no-store; Range/206 supported for seeking; strict CSP on all responses so scripts inside SVG cannot run on the site domain.

nodes.label: Archive Over Delete
nodes.rationale: Media is referenced from 12 places; archiving hides a file from the library while existing references keep working. Deleting an in-use file returns 409 with the exact usage list, because blind deletion means broken images and unplayable video on live pages.

nodes.label: AccessService Entitlement Check
nodes.rationale: Entitlement can come from four sources and is evaluated in exactly one place, not scattered to clients — otherwise the mobile app, the site and the backend would each answer differently. A one-off purchase never grants casting-project access; only active Premium does.

nodes.label: Server-Built Homepage Feed
nodes.rationale: GET /api/v1/app/home builds the mobile home screen server-side (TZ §31) so adding or reordering a row does not require a new store release. Row order is two-stage (explicit item list wins, otherwise automatic newest-first), section order is changed in one request to avoid an intermediate mixed state, and empty sections are omitted rather than rendered as headerless rows.

nodes.label: Watch Entitlement Endpoint
nodes.rationale: Returns whether playback is allowed, a reason, a requiredAction and prices. When denied, `sources` is empty — a video link is never shipped alongside a refusal — and the file endpoint checks independently, making protection two-layered.

nodes.label: In-Memory Rate Limiting
nodes.rationale: Token bucket per IP running before the Spring Security chain; exceeding returns 429 with Retry-After. In-memory, so it only covers a single instance — multiple instances would need Redis.

nodes.label: Public Endpoint Allowlist
nodes.rationale: All /api/** is closed except an explicitly enumerated list. casting-user/my/** and /appeal/** remain open only because the Telegram bot flow has no authentication; closing them requires agreement with the bot team.

nodes.label: Telegram Bot Integration
nodes.rationale: The bot posts casting applications (POST /api/v1/casting-user) and uploads photos (POST /api/v1/file/upload) without authentication, which is why those endpoints stay public.

nodes.label: Message Entity Is Not A Messenger
nodes.rationale: The legacy `Message` entity is the accepted/rejected reply sent to the Telegram bot, not chat. Deleting it would mean candidates never receive an answer.

nodes.label: Deliberate Known Limitations
nodes.rationale: FCM has no key (503 and a FAILED record rather than a fake 'sent'), payment providers are unconnected and the store-billing risk is unresolved, Stars/Coin rate is unset so donation revenue reports null rather than a guess, dev videos are 256 KB of random bytes, search is LIKE '%text%', and the rate limiter is in-memory. Nothing is faked as working.

hyperedges.label: Four Entitlement Sources Converging On AccessService
